A.  FY 2024-25 BUDGET PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council take the following actions: 1) Open the Public
  Hearing and take any public testimony related to the budget adoption, including fees
  and charges, fund balance policy, investment policy, and pension funding policy; 2)
  Close the Public Hearing; 3) Review and adopt: a. Resolution 2573 - Adopting the
  Consolidated Budget; b. Resolution 2574 - Adopting the City’s Gann Appropriations
  Limit; c. Resolution 2575 - Adopting the Schedule of Municipal Fees and Charges; d.
  Statement of Fund Balance Policy, Statement of Investment Policy, and Statement of
  Pension Funding Policy.

City Manager Grammer summarized that the proposed budget incorporates direction
provided to staff by the City Council at the Budget Study Session on May 28, 2024, as well
as direction from the Finance/Audit Subcommittee comprised of MAYOR SCHMITZ and
MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA, who met with staff on May 7, 2024. The 2024-25 budget
provides conservative but realistic revenue assumptions and plans for expenditures for
essential services and capital projects that benefit the entire community. It also reflects
healthy reserves and is consistent with the City’s investment policy, pension funding policy
and fund balance policy.

Senior Accountant Estrada provided a summary of the staff report (as per the staff report).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3

   749; 5) Continue the Public Hearing for a second reading and adoption of Ordinance
  No. 749, to the City Council meeting of July 9, 2024.

Senior Planner provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Senior Planner Berry explained that the Commercial Limited Mixed-Use District (CLMU)
designation at the site of The General Store and Kelly’s Korner allows for uses such as retail,
and the landmark overlay addresses new development and modifications of the structures
on the site, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN discussion ensued about the workforce housing on
School District properties.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA thanked staff and the Planning Commission for the clear
concise amendments and presentation to the zoning code. She agreed that strengthening
the landmark overlay designation would be a good idea and noted that there are only two
sites in the City designated as Commercial Limited Mixed-Use District (CLMU). She also
explained how important it is to have workforce housing available for the people who work
in this community, especially teachers and first responders.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from California Housing Defense Fund and Grant Mogford, as
well as Devin Serrano, Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District Superintendent.

Discussion ensued about workforce housing, the fact that the School District does not have
any immediate plans to build workforce housing at this time.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  CONTINUED THE PUBLIC HEARING FOR A SECOND READING AND
  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 749, TO THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF
  JULY 9, 2024.
